title: Darjeeling on a budget: a good trip for less
meta_description: How to do Darjeeling for ₹1,800–3,000 a day: shared jeeps, WBTDC and family-run rooms, momo-and-thali meals, free views and the add-ons worth skipping.
summary: A careful traveller can do Darjeeling for about ₹1,800–3,000 a person a day, indicative 2026. The savings come from shared jeeps instead of reserved cars, a room near Chowrasta so you walk everywhere, local food, one paid Tiger Hill morning on a clear day, and avoiding the May–June and Puja peaks.

sections.heading: Where the money actually goes
paras: Darjeeling is not an expensive town. Rooms, food and entry fees are all modest by Indian hill-station standards. What breaks budgets is the car. A reserved car from Bagdogra, a three-point sightseeing tour, a five-point tour, a Mirik day trip and a drop back to the plains can easily cost a family ₹15,000–20,000 before anyone has eaten a momo. A couple can halve their trip cost just by riding the shared jeeps that local people use every day.

Here is what a frugal day and a comfortable day look like per person, sharing a room. These are indicative 2026 ranges. Prices rise in May, June and the Durga Puja to Diwali weeks, and fall sharply in July, August and January.

sections.heading: Getting up the hill for under ₹400
paras: Shared jeeps, usually Tata Sumos and Mahindra Boleros, wait outside NJP station and at the stands along Hill Cart Road in Siliguri. A seat to Darjeeling costs ₹250–400, indicative 2026, and the trip takes 3–3.5 hours. Jeeps leave when full, which in the morning means every few minutes. After about 2 pm departures thin out, and drivers may ask you to pay for the empty seats. Jeeps arrive at the motor stands near Chowk Bazaar, below the main town; from there it is a steep 10–15 minute walk to Chowrasta, or a porter for ₹100–200.

If you fly into Bagdogra, take an app cab or a shared auto to Siliguri town or the NJP area and pick up a jeep there; it still beats a reserved airport car for a couple. A family of four or five should compare: a reserved car at ₹3,500–4,500 costs much the same as five jeep seats and saves time with luggage. Fares follow fuel prices, so check current status before you travel.
Buy your return seat at the motor stand the afternoon before you leave. Ask for the middle row; the back rows are cramped and bouncy on the bends.

sections.heading: Cheap rooms that are not bad rooms
paras: Location saves more than a low room rate. A room within 10 minutes' walk of Chowrasta, along Gandhi Road, Laden La Road, Dr Zakir Hussain Road or around the Mall, means you never need a taxi in town. Rooms far down the Hill Cart Road or out towards Ghum look cheap online and then cost you ₹150–300 a day in taxis and an hour a day climbing.

The West Bengal tourism corporation's Darjeeling Tourism Property on Bhanu Sarani, just above Chowrasta, has plain rooms at government rates, roughly ₹2,300–3,500 a room night, and on clear mornings a direct view towards Kangchenjunga. Small family-run places such as Revolver, a short walk below Chowrasta, cost ₹1,800–3,000. In the off-season many guesthouses on the lanes around Dr Zakir Hussain Road go below ₹1,500.

Before you book, ask three questions. Is there hot water all day, or only at set hours? Is there a heater or electric blanket from November to February? How many steps from the road? Darjeeling is built on a ridge, and a cheap room up 90 steps is no bargain with suitcases. Walk-in rates in the low season are often lower than website rates; ask.

sections.heading: Eating well for ₹400–600 a day
paras: Darjeeling eats cheaply and well. A plate of momos costs ₹60–150, a bowl of thukpa ₹80–180, a plate of aloo dum ₹30–60 and a vegetarian thali with rice, dal, a vegetable and pickle ₹120–250, indicative 2026. The best prices are in the lanes below Nehru Road, around Chowk Bazaar and near the motor stands, where office workers and drivers eat. The cafes and restaurants on Chowrasta and the Mall charge for the view.

Breakfast is the easy saving. A hotel breakfast can cost ₹250–450. A tea stall with sel roti, the ring-shaped Nepali rice bread, or puri and aloo, with milky tea, feeds you for ₹60–100. Carry a refillable bottle; most hotels will fill it from a filter, saving ₹60–100 a day.
Tea, of course, is the one thing worth spending on. A cup of a named garden's first flush at a tea room costs ₹80–250, and it is the best value luxury in town.

sections.heading: Free and nearly free Darjeeling
paras: Many of the best hours here cost nothing. These are the ones we send budget travellers to first. Fees, where they exist, change from time to time, so treat them as indicative.
list: Chowrasta at 6 am: on a clear morning Kangchenjunga fills the northern sky. Free, and often as good as Tiger Hill.
The Mall loop round Observatory Hill, about 1.5 km and car-free, with the Mahakal temple at the top. Free.
St Andrew's Church above Chowrasta, built in 1843 and rebuilt in 1873. Free; quiet inside.
Ghum and Batasia Loop by shared jeep for ₹30–60 a seat, with Batasia entry at ₹20–50, instead of a ₹1,500 car.
Yiga Choeling monastery in Ghum, founded in 1850. Free; a small offering at the altar is welcome.
Happy Valley Tea Estate, a 3 km downhill walk from Chowrasta. Garden entry and tasting ₹100–300.
The Japanese Peace Pagoda on Jalapahar, opened in 1992. Free, with a good view back over the town.
Watching the toy train pass through Ghum or the bazaar near the station. Free, if you ask your hotel for the day's timings.

sections.heading: Sightseeing: where to spend, where to cut
paras: The standard local tours are sold as three-point (Tiger Hill, Ghum, Batasia) and seven-point (the zoo and HMI, ropeway, Tibetan centre, tea garden, Peace Pagoda and others). A three-point car costs ₹1,500–2,200 and a seven-point car ₹2,500–3,500, indicative 2026. Split four ways, the three-point is fair value. The seven-point is poor value for a couple: most of its stops are walkable or a ₹20–40 shared taxi away.

Spend on the things you cannot do cheaply another way: one Tiger Hill morning, and only when the forecast is clear; the toy-train joyride, if the train matters to you; and the zoo and Himalayan Mountaineering Institute combined ticket, ₹100–150, which is one of the best-value mornings in the hills. Cut the pony rides, the costume photos on Chowrasta and the hotel-booked Mirik car if you can reach Mirik by shared jeep for ₹150–250.

sections.heading: When to go for the lowest prices
paras: Rates follow school holidays across eastern India and Bangladesh. Late April to mid-June and the Durga Puja to Diwali weeks are the dearest, and Christmas to New Year is busy. The cheapest months are July and August, with rain, cloud and landslide risk, and January to February, with cold nights but often the clearest skies of the year.

Our pick for budget travellers is the first half of March or the second half of November to early December. Views are good on many mornings, crowds are thin and hotels still bargain. Avoid the days of a bandh or strike, which still happen occasionally; follow local news and check current status before you travel.

A three-night plan we give students: day one, shared jeep up and an evening on the Mall; day two, Ghum and Batasia by shared jeep, then the zoo and HMI on foot; day three, Happy Valley and the Peace Pagoda on foot; day four, Chowrasta at dawn and the jeep down. Transport for the whole trip comes to about ₹800–1,200 per person, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: How much does a 3-day Darjeeling trip cost on a budget
faqs.a: About ₹6,000–9,000 per person for three nights, twin sharing, indicative 2026, using shared jeeps from NJP, a budget room near Chowrasta, local food and one shared Tiger Hill morning. Add ₹800–1,600 for a toy-train joyride. Our 2-night budget package starts around ₹6,500 per person with transfers and the Tiger Hill trip arranged.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way from NJP to Darjeeling
faqs.a: A shared jeep seat for ₹250–400, indicative 2026, from outside NJP station or the Siliguri stands on Hill Cart Road. It takes 3–3.5 hours. Go before 2 pm, when departures thin out. Buses run from Siliguri too, slower but sometimes cheaper. Fares change with fuel prices, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Tiger Hill worth paying for
faqs.a: Only on a clear morning. A shared seat costs ₹300–500 and a car ₹1,500–2,200, indicative 2026. On a cloudy day you see nothing after a 4 am start. Check the sky and forecast the evening before. If it looks doubtful, go to Chowrasta or Observatory Hill at 6 am instead, which is free and often gives a fine view.

faqs.q: Which month is cheapest for Darjeeling
faqs.a: July and August are cheapest, with heavy discounts, but rain and cloud hide the mountains and landslides slow the roads. January and February are also cheap and often very clear, though cold. For low prices and reliable views, choose the first half of March or the second half of November.

faqs.q: Can I see Darjeeling without hiring a car
faqs.a: Yes. Chowrasta, the Mall, Observatory Hill, the zoo and HMI, the Tibetan centre, St Andrew's Church, Happy Valley and the bazaar are all walkable. Shared jeeps reach Ghum and Batasia for ₹30–60 a seat. You only really need a car for Tiger Hill at dawn, and even there shared seats are sold in season.

faqs.q: What do momos cost in Darjeeling
faqs.a: About ₹60–150 a plate, indicative 2026, depending on the filling and the place. Vegetable momos are cheapest, chicken and pork cost more. Small eateries below Nehru Road and around Chowk Bazaar charge less than cafes on the Mall. A bowl of thukpa costs ₹80–180 and a thali ₹120–250.

faqs.q: Is the WBTDC lodge in Darjeeling good value
faqs.a: Yes, for location and price. The Darjeeling Tourism Property sits just above Chowrasta, so you walk everywhere, and rooms cost roughly ₹2,300–3,500 a night, indicative. Rooms and bathrooms are dated and service is government style. Book on the WBTDCL website well ahead for October and May.

faqs.q: Is the toy-train joyride worth it on a budget
faqs.a: If the train is a reason you came, yes: the diesel joyride costs ₹800–1,000, indicative 2026, and gives you two hours on a UNESCO-listed line with stops at Batasia Loop and the Ghum museum. If not, watch the train pass in Ghum or Batasia for free or for a small entry fee.

faqs.q: Do Darjeeling hotels give off-season discounts
faqs.a: Yes. From July to September and from January to early March, many hotels cut rates by 20–40 percent, and some small guesthouses more. Ask for the walk-in or direct rate rather than the website rate, and offer to pay in cash or by UPI. Discounts are smaller in the second half of December.
